w_rusted_sword: Under the rust near the guard there is a maker's stamp, struck out with a chisel. Whoever armed you did not want the forge known.
w_knight_sword: The garrison numbered its blades. This one is four hundred and twelve; the roll it was entered in stops at four hundred.
w_ashen_great: The scorch is not from one fire. It was laid on in layers, a watch at a time, by something that never set it down to rest.
w_woodcutter: The Blackwood does not take an edge kindly. The haft has been replaced nine times, and each time from the same tree.
w_headsman: The Executioner kept a tally on the haft. Every notch is shallow, as if cut by a hand that hoped to be stopped.
w_twin_fangs: They were a wedding gift, one for each hand of the bride. The Widow had the second inscription ground away the same night.
w_pilgrim_blades: Pilgrims were forbidden swords on the Cathedral road. Nobody thought to forbid them two knives.
w_censer_sword: The incense was burned for the dead of a single night. There was enough ash to quench a hundred blades; they made only this one.
w_crypt_great: It was buried with its first owner and dug up by its second. The Gravewarden considered that a loan and came to collect.
w_frost_great: The King passed sentence with it resting across his knees. In the Citadel's records no verdict after the first winter is an acquittal.
w_rime_sword: The smiths worked with the doors open so the cold would do the tempering. Three of them finished it. One signed it.
w_monarch: It is older than the throne and was not made for it. The grip was shortened, once, to fit a hand smaller than the first.
w_oath_axe: An oath was sworn on it and kept for a lifetime. It was the lifetime after that one which gave the axe its name.
w_ember_fangs: Quench them and they cool for an hour. Whatever keeps them lit is in the metal and is not, strictly, fire.
w_wyrmfang: The wyrm shed it; nobody took it. The hilt-maker's notes say the tooth hummed whenever the Roost was mentioned aloud.
w_hunger: Weigh them before a fight and after. The difference is small, and it is never in the direction you expect.
w_dawnline: Made for a ceremony at first light that has not been held since. The edge was an afterthought, and a good one.
w_vigil_edge: Each watchman scratched a line inside the scabbard at the end of a watch. The lines run out long before the blade's wear does.
w_starfall: It will not hold a magnet and it does not ring when struck. Orren says it was not forged so much as persuaded.
w_throneshard: The seat was never stone. Where the shard was cut away there are fine bright threads, all leading down.
